title: Working with REST APIs 🤖
description: Interact with RESTful services – parse JSON, authenticate with tokens/keys, and consume real‑world APIs.

slides.title: What is a REST API?
slides.content:
# Application Programming Interface

A REST API exposes server functionality over HTTP using standard methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). Data is usually returned as **JSON**.

Example: GitHub API `https://api.github.com/users/octocat` returns JSON with user details.

Hacking tools often consume APIs for reconnaissance, searching exploits, or automating tasks.

slides.title: Calling an API
slides.content: Fetch public data from a free API:
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
resp = requests.get('https://api.github.com/users/octocat')
if resp.status_code == 200:
    data = resp.json()  # parse JSON into dict
    print(f"Name: {data['name']}")
    print(f"Public repos: {data['public_repos']}")

quizData.question: What does `resp.json()` do?

options.text: Parses the response body as JSON and returns a Python dict/list

quizData.explanation: It deserializes JSON into Python objects.

slides.title: API Authentication
slides.content:
# Most APIs Require a Key or Token

* **Query parameter**: `?api_key=YOUR_KEY`
* **Header**: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN` or `X-API-Key: ...`

```python
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ghp_xxxxxxxxx'}
resp = requests.get('https://api.github.com/user', headers=headers)
```
Never hardcode keys! Use environment variables or config files.

slides.title: Using Environment Variable for API Key

quizData.question: It's safe to commit your API keys to a public GitHub repository if the code is open source.
quizData.explanation: Never expose secrets; attackers scan for them. Use environment variables or secret management.

slides.title: Pagination – Getting All Results
slides.content:
# APIs Often Return Limited Results Per Page

They provide a `next` link or a `page` parameter. You must loop until no more data.

```python
url = 'https://api.example.com/data?page=1'
while url:
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
    data = resp.json()
    process(data['results'])
    url = data.get('next')  # None if last page
```
This is critical for scraping large datasets.

slides.title: Sending Data to an API (POST/PUT)
slides.content:
# Create or Update Resources

```python
new_repo = {"name": "my-hacking-tool", "private": False}
resp = requests.post('https://api.github.com/user/repos', json=new_repo, headers=headers)
if resp.status_code == 201:
    print("Repository created")
```
Always check the API documentation for required fields and format.

quizData.question: Which HTTP method would you use to update an existing resource via a REST API?
quizData.explanation: PUT replaces the entire resource; PATCH modifies part of it.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Rate Limiting

Many APIs limit requests per minute. If you exceed, you'll get 429 Too Many Requests. Implement delays and handle retries gracefully.
